scope: Corollary 4.3 (Shears, pairs, and embedded words) of the manuscript “Finite tensor savings and exact Fourier circuits” (preprints/Finite-tensor-savings-and-exact-Fourier-circuits-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 130 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e2165b9f6796f018), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every nontrivial elementary coordinate shear has price one, including with any number of untouched coordinates. Every invertible 2×2 matrix has price at most two. If a word on w coordinates implements G, using nonmonomial calls A1, . . . , Al and monomials, then p(G) ≤ l X j=1 p(Aj). If the word instead implements G ⊕ Is, the same bound holds for p(G), with no restriction on the initial values of the s coordinates restored by the word.
